result.note: Tests the direction and composition of June 2026 merchandise trade data and the May 2026 gold import duty hike.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's merchandise trade data for June 2026, released by the Commerce Ministry in July 2026:
items: The merchandise trade deficit widened to USD 30.43 billion, a five-month high.
Merchandise exports grew faster than merchandise imports year-on-year.
Merchandise exports were led by gems, jewellery and engineering goods.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Exports rose 15.5% to USD 40.41 billion, while imports grew almost twice as fast, up 31% to USD 70.84 billion. The government attributed the larger import bill to higher global prices for crude and precious metals rather than to rising volumes.
questions.source: Merchandise exports rose 15.5% year-on-year in June to USD 40.41 billion, led by gems, jewellery, and engineering goods.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, the Centre raised the import duty on gold from 6% to which rate?
questions.explain: The duty was raised to 15% two days after the Prime Minister asked citizens to pause gold purchases and foreign holidays for a year to conserve foreign exchange. Gold imports still jumped 47% in June 2026 to USD 1.96 billion.
questions.source: Two days later, the Centre raised the gold import duty from 6% to 15%.
